angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 7,050,224 km at 65.57 pc = 1.44 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 111710: distance 65.574 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.014), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 65.574 +/- 0.918 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 14.7149 +/- 0.0995 mas (same row, RUWE 0.94), 147.8 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 10.134 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 111710: radius 10.134 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 43.36 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.055) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 7,050,224 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4656 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 111710: effective temperature 4656 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.099) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 111710: effective temperature 4656 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.099) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
